column1: # GE-T11's planted far contradictions (SMYSL-2.4 §6 TX-P7 step 3).
# Fifty pairs. Each row is one contradiction: two claims that cannot both be true, written in
# the idiom of ../bibles/slice/eng-kjv/ so that they compete with that corpus's own vocabulary
# rather than standing out from it, and placed at locators in two different books so that no
# adjacency rule can reach from one to the other. That is what GE-T11 means by *far*.
# WHO WROTE THESE. A person did, by hand, which is the thing to know before reading the figure
# they produce. A planted set written by the same hand that wrote the generator is a set whose
# difficulty that hand chose, and the honest reading of a recall measured over it is "the
# instrument works", not "the linker finds contradictions in the wild". The deliberate counter
# is in the wording: no pair repeats its partner's content words where a different word would
# do, because a pair that shared every term would be measuring string equality.
#   id        a stable name for the pair, so a disagreement can be argued about by name
#   lang      the language both halves are written in (the lexical source groups by it)
#   at_a      the locator the first half is cited at
#   at_b      the locator the second half is cited at
#   gist_b    the second claim, which cannot hold if the first does
# An external set replaces this one through SMYSL_GE_T11_PLANTED=<file>, and the distractor
# corpus through SMYSL_GE_T11_CORPUS=<dir of *.smy>. Both are how the figure gets a denominator
# this repository is too small to hold.

column4: gist_a
column6: gist_b

column4: A famine lay upon the land in the days when the judges ruled
column6: The land yielded her increase without fail throughout the years of the judges

column4: A man of Beth-lehem-judah departed to dwell in the country of Moab
column6: No household of Beth-lehem-judah ever crossed over into Moab

column4: Elimelech the husband of Naomi came to his end
column6: Elimelech outlived every man of his generation

column4: Naomi was the mother of two sons
column6: Naomi bore no children at all

column4: Mahlon and Chilion both perished in Moab
column6: The sons of Naomi returned alive to Judah with their mother

column4: They dwelled in that country about ten years
column6: Their stay in that country lasted scarcely a single season

column4: The sons took to themselves wives of the women of Moab
column6: Neither son took any wife while he lived

column4: Orpah kissed her mother in law and turned back
column6: Orpah clave unto Naomi and would not be parted from her

column4: Ruth refused to leave Naomi and clave unto her
column6: Ruth departed to her own people and was seen no more

column4: Naomi bade her daughters in law return each to her mother's house
column6: Naomi commanded the two women to follow her and never turn aside

column4: Naomi said she was too old to have a husband
column6: Naomi was yet a young woman with her years before her

column4: Word came to Moab that the LORD had given his people bread
column6: The dearth in Judah held fast and no report of bread went out

column4: Naomi set out on the way to return unto the land of Judah
column6: Naomi remained in Moab to the end of her days

column4: All the city was moved at their coming to Beth-lehem
column6: They entered the town unremarked and none took notice of them

column4: Naomi asked to be called Mara, for she went out full and came home empty
column6: Naomi came home laden, and her name was kept as it had always been

column4: They came to Beth-lehem at the beginning of barley harvest
column6: Their arrival fell long after every field was reaped and bare

column4: Boaz was a kinsman of the husband of Naomi
column6: Boaz was a stranger to that family and of no kin to them

column4: Ruth went into the field to glean ears of corn after the reapers
column6: Ruth never set foot in any field of that country

column4: Boaz came from Beth-lehem and saluted the reapers
column6: Boaz sent no word to his reapers and did not come among them

column4: Boaz asked his servant whose damsel the young woman was
column6: Boaz took no interest in who laboured in his field

column4: Boaz charged Ruth to go to no other field but abide by his maidens
column6: Boaz told her she was free to glean in whatever field she chose

column4: Ruth was given leave to drink of that which the young men had drawn
column6: Ruth was forbidden the water of that household

column4: All that Ruth had done for her mother in law was fully reported to Boaz
column6: What she had done was kept from Boaz and he heard nothing of it

column4: Boaz blessed her as one come to trust under the wings of the LORD
column6: Boaz cursed her coming and called her trust a vain thing

column4: Ruth said she was not like unto one of his handmaidens
column6: Ruth claimed the standing of his handmaidens as her own right

column4: She did eat and was sufficed and left some over
column6: She ate nothing at that meal and went away hungry

column4: Boaz commanded that handfuls be let fall on purpose for her
column6: Boaz ordered the reapers to leave her nothing beyond the common gleaning

column4: What she had gleaned was about an ephah of barley
column6: Her gleaning amounted to no more than a few ears

column4: Naomi asked where Ruth had gleaned that day
column6: Naomi asked her nothing, being indifferent where she had been

column4: Naomi said the man was near of kin, one of their next kinsmen
column6: Naomi said no kinsman remained to them in all the land

column4: Ruth kept fast by the maidens of Boaz unto the end of wheat harvest
column6: Ruth left his service in the first week and did not return

column4: Naomi sought rest for Ruth that it might be well with her
column6: Naomi made no provision for her and left her to her own devices

column4: Boaz winnowed barley in the threshingfloor that night
column6: The floor stood empty that night and no winnowing was done

column4: Ruth said she would do all that her mother in law bade her
column6: Ruth refused the counsel she was given and did otherwise

column4: At midnight the man was afraid and turned himself
column6: He slept unbroken until the morning and was never startled

column4: Ruth asked Boaz to spread his skirt over his handmaid
column6: Ruth asked nothing of him and made no request at all

column4: The city knew Ruth for a virtuous woman
column6: Her name was ill spoken of throughout the town

column4: There was a kinsman nearer than Boaz
column6: Boaz stood nearest of all and none came before him

column4: Boaz measured six measures of barley and laid it on her
column6: He sent her away from the floor with empty hands

column4: Ruth was told not to go empty unto her mother in law
column6: She was charged to carry nothing back with her

column4: Ten men of the elders of the city sat down in the gate
column6: No elders were gathered and the gate stood deserted

column4: Naomi sold the parcel of land that was Elimelech's
column6: That parcel was never offered and remained unsold

column4: The nearer kinsman said at first that he would redeem it
column6: He refused from the beginning and never spoke of redeeming

column4: The kinsman said he could not redeem it lest he mar his own inheritance
column6: He redeemed it gladly and counted his inheritance untouched

column4: A man plucked off his shoe to confirm the thing in Israel
column6: No sign or token was used, the word alone standing for the bargain

column4: Boaz bought all that was Elimelech's of the hand of Naomi
column6: Nothing of that estate passed to Boaz

column4: All the people in the gate said they were witnesses
column6: The matter was done in secret with no witness to it

column4: Boaz took Ruth and she became his wife
column6: Boaz never married, and Ruth remained a widow

column4: Ruth bore a son, and the women called his name Obed
column6: Ruth died childless and no son was born to her

column4: Obed begat Jesse, and Jesse begat David
column6: The line failed with Obed and went no further
